key_insight: CFD-driven symbolic regression learns compact, interpretable corrections to a RANS transition model that improve predictions beyond the flat-plate training cases.
engineering_relevance: More accurate transition modeling can improve turbine heat-transfer and loss predictions, with heat-transfer errors reduced by up to 70% in the tested LS89 cascade cases.
method: Learn bounded, closed-form corrections to production and destruction activation functions in the k–ω–γ intermittency equation.
Optimize coefficients with a RANS solver in the loop, accelerated by POD-Kriging field surrogates.
Select elastic-net hyperparameters through bi-level optimization and leave-one-case-out validation, retaining 11 of 21 candidate terms.
evidence_signal: Training used wall-resolved LES mean-velocity data for ERCOFTAC T3 flat plates; testing without retraining improved LS89 turbine heat-transfer predictions at all four operating points.
watch_item: Residual errors in transition onset and length indicate that flat-plate-only training limits accuracy in more complex turbine flows.
paper_title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
